clue.text: Display knitwear for equestrians

parts.note: to show is to put on display
jumpers are knitted pullovers, the British word for sweaters

explanation.surface: A shop window arranges woollens aimed at horse riders.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders who compete in the sport of jumping horses over fences are known by this compound name.

clue.text: The first person to play piano, I noted, has a high regard for his ability

definitions.text: has a high regard for his ability

parts.note: the self is the first person, the 'I' of grammar

indicators.note: the letters are made to play about, freely rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A conceited pianist writes himself first on the programme to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of the kind of person, read as 'one who has a high regard for his ability'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone conceited, convinced of their own views and talents, is described by this hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Love to change the organ

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Romance can alter a church instrument, or so the line suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The ovary is the female reproductive organ that produces eggs.

clue.text: Green-eyed Jack keen to remove the last character

indicators.note: Jack is set to remove a letter and stand in its place, a swap of one letter for another

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A man named Jack, envious, wants to oust whoever came last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last character' sounds like the end of a word, but it means the last letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Green-eyed is an idiom for envy, from Shakespeare's 'green-eyed monster' in Othello.

clue.text: Humble, sound English dressmaker

indicators.note: sound here means 'as heard', so the word for humble is taken by how it is spoken

explanation.surface: A modest, reliable English seamstress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it signals that the word is taken by how it is pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A modiste is a fashionable milliner or maker of dresses, a word borrowed from French.

clue.text: Obliquely gaining advantage over sage

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits over the other, so it comes first

explanation.surface: Getting the better of a wise old person by an indirect route.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgewise means sideways, with the edge foremost, which is moving at a slant.

clue.text: Mass production affecting transport, for example

parts.note: a Mass is a church service
industry is the production of goods

explanation.surface: Mass manufacturing has an effect on the transport sector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass production' reads as one phrase, but Mass is the church rite.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport is an example of a sector that sells services rather than goods, the business category named here.

clue.text: No time for descant to change and rise

indicators.note: the remaining letters change, being put in a new order
no time means the letter for time is not wanted, so it is dropped

explanation.surface: A choir has no time to alter the descant before it soars.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to go up, a direct synonym of rise.

clue.text: Small reduction on unusual stencil for buyer

indicators.note: the leftover letters are made unusual, set in an unfamiliar order
a reduction on the word means a letter is cut from it

explanation.surface: A shop offers a small discount on an odd stencil to tempt a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a price cut; it is a letter cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is a customer, someone who buys goods or services.

clue.text: Lieutenant in sauna cavorting with potentate's lady

indicators.note: the officer is placed in the jumbled letters
cavorting means leaping about, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: An army officer frolics in a steam room with a ruler's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is the wife of a sultan, the ruler of a Muslim state.

clue.text: Foolish lodger receiving note in rhyme

indicators.note: the jumbled word receives a letter into its middle
the letters are made foolish, scrambled into nonsense

explanation.surface: A silly tenant takes in a musical note and turns it into verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel, also spelt this way, is crude or trivial verse, a word for poor rhyme.

clue.text: Mouse scuttling round small horse, from which the title is derived

definitions.text: from which the title is derived

indicators.note: the mouse's letters go round the horse, surrounding it
scuttling suggests scurrying about, so the letters scurry into a new order

parts.note: a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: A mouse darts around a little horse, as in a children's story named after its hero.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponymous character is the one whose name gives a work its title, such as Hamlet.

clue.text: Husband in drink makes high-pitched noise

indicators.note: the husband is put in the drink

explanation.surface: A drunk husband starts squealing.
explanation.definitionFit: To whine is to give a long high-pitched complaining cry.

clue.text: Part of the agenda is revised at this stage

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, letters lying inside it

parts.note: the platform's letters run across the end of agenda and the word is

explanation.surface: A meeting's agenda gets revised at this point in proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At this stage' sounds like 'now'; the stage is a platform where a revised agenda might be presented.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform in a hall, a small stage for speakers.

clue.text: Evaluation: assent to be given when internal mess sorted

indicators.note: assent is given something that is internal, held inside it
the mess is sorted out, put into a new order

explanation.surface: An appraisal: approval is granted once the office muddle has been tidied.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is a judgement of value or quality, the same as an evaluation.

clue.text: Hold back the rest dancing in the rain

parts.note: taken as written, the word rest

explanation.surface: Stop the others from dancing about in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' looks like an anagram signal, but the two words simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or keep under control.

clue.text: Newly-wed German has room for partner

parts.note: a bride is a woman newly married

explanation.surface: A recently married German makes space for a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly-wed' looks like the definition, but it is only the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom is the man getting married, the bride's partner.

clue.text: Old student turns up to gamble in a camisole

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil
to dice is to gamble with dice

explanation.surface: A former pupil arrives to bet while wearing a lacy top.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the close-fitting upper part of a dress, like a camisole, a sleeveless undergarment.

clue.text: Pronounced dead, toes turned up, but makes a sharp reply

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is said over the dead

indicators.note: the toes are turned over, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Declared dead with feet in the air, the corpse still gets in a quick retort.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'turn up one's toes' is slang for dying, which ties the surface together.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick retort; as a verb it means to answer back smartly, from a fencing thrust.

clue.text: It's nothing to see four parts rosso in fortified wine

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: only four of the word's five letters are used, one being dropped

parts.note: rosso is Italian for red, as in red wine

explanation.surface: Mixing a little red wine into something stronger seems a non-event.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark, rich style of sherry, which is a fortified wine from Spain.

clue.text: Social climber initially somewhat naively off balance

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words, read in order

explanation.surface: An upwardly mobile type falls over, somewhat naive in their striving.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob looks down on those of lower status and imitates those above, the classic social climber.

clue.text: Valediction for a blackbird?

parts.note: the blackbird recalls a 1926 popular song whose title bids that bird farewell

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the farewell comes from the title of the 1926 song 'Bye Bye Blackbird'.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled word is an informal goodbye, so it is a farewell, as in the famous song.

clue.text: Party with Hazel, perhaps, having cake from America

parts.note: a hazel is an example of a nut

explanation.surface: At a celebration, a woman called Hazel has a slice of American cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel looks like a woman's name; it is the nut tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the American spelling of the ring-shaped fried cake the British write doughnut.

clue.text: Sue, during exercise, went up to dock

indicators.note: the inner pieces happen during the exercise, set inside it

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
to dock is to cut, as a tail is docked

explanation.surface: A woman named Sue climbed up to a ship's berth while working out.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue looks like a name; it is the definition, meaning to take to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosecute is to bring legal proceedings against someone, which is to sue.

clue.text: Quits at about seven

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stops work at roughly seven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quits' looks like a verb about leaving; it is the adjective meaning square with no debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means neither side owes the other, which is the same as being level or square.

clue.text: Ignore girl with weapon

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them

explanation.surface: Snub a young woman who is armed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword, as carried by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: In open view, secretly remove key

indicators.note: the key is removed, a letter taken away

explanation.surface: Openly, someone sneaks off with a key.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs open view with secrecy, which is the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtly means done openly and publicly, not hidden.

clue.text: Unorthodox lady surgeon acting in a way that's risky

indicators.note: the letters are made unorthodox, put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A maverick female surgeon operates with reckless abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangerously describes acting with hazard or peril, which matches doing something risky.
